completed_protein_followup.vs_released_pvb: Both final base seeds and time71 retain worse protein bond, angle, clash, MSD, RMSF and whole CA position/distance-path scores with positive marginal intervals. Some increment scores improve; this does not establish overall better motion.
completed_protein_followup.interpretation: The geometry/motion tradeoff is observed across both molecular domains, with seed-dependent learning curves. Direct-time modulation improves same-step protein geometry and whole CA paths but worsens MSD/RMSF and CA increments. Its capacity, conditioning and seed dependence remain unresolved; correct interval response is still unproven.

learning_curve_conclusion: Seed71 improves bonds and some whole paths but worsens RMSF with more updates; seed72 worsens bonds/pocket paths while slightly improving RMSF. Therefore more training is neither uniformly harmful nor a stable joint improvement under this recipe. Do not generalize the earlier seed72 finding into a universal claim. Both final seeds remain worse than released PVB in bonds with positive marginal paired intervals.

time_interpretation: Direct physical-time FiLM shows a mixed first-seed result, not a repaired clock response. Added parameters and architectural conditioning both change; this is not a parameter-count-matched time-input placebo. decision: No promotion and no blind extra updates. Continue already-running time-interleaving and endpoint-geometry matched experiments; finish final and second-seed evidence. Preserve every declared seed and checkpoint result rather than selecting the best.
